entries.label: Tropical/Subtropical lowland rainforests
entries.reviewNote: Water balance, layered canopy, productivity and resource cycling need quantified and causal rules; tropical is not a latitude-only test.

entries.label: Deciduous temperate forests
entries.reviewNote: Canopy share, temperature seasonality, growing season and soil fertility remain unquantified; no tree species is universally required.

entries.label: Temperate pyric humid forests
entries.reviewNote: Fire regime, tall multilayer structure and summer drought episodes need explicit recurrence, severity and succession semantics.

entries.label: Temperate pyric sclerophyll forests and woodlands
entries.reviewNote: Quantified water deficit, nutrients and fire intervals are not encoded; a recent burn is not evidence of a pyric ecosystem by itself.

entries.label: Temperate subhumid grasslands
entries.reviewNote: Seasonal water balance, C3/C4 traits, soil properties, disturbance and tree-exclusion mechanisms need review.

entries.label: Annual croplands
entries.reviewNote: Annual management cycle and resource subsidies need temporal rules; high-input practice is not a universal numeric threshold here.

entries.label: Permanent marshes
entries.reviewNote: Water depth, anoxia, nutrients and marsh physiognomy remain qualitative; permanent inundation is not exhaustive water cover.

entries.label: Seasonal floodplain marshes
entries.reviewNote: Flooding then exposure is a schematic recurring cycle; durations, gaps, spatial extent and interannual variation are unspecified. No equal phase length is assumed.

entries.label: Boreal, temperate and montane peat bogs
entries.reviewNote: GET bogs must not all be narrowed to strictly ombrotrophic raised bogs; peat chemistry and formation feedbacks need separate constraints.

entries.label: Boreal and temperate fens
entries.reviewNote: Mineral-water input, productivity, anoxia and water-table regime matter; rich and poor fens must remain possible regional refinements.

entries.label: Permanent upland streams
entries.reviewNote: Stream order, slope, velocity, oxygen and catchment subsidies are not executable; perennial is not constant discharge.

entries.label: Seasonal upland streams
entries.reviewNote: This GET group may include perennial flows as well as intermittent streams. Seasonal must not be interpreted as obligatory dry-channel absence.

entries.label: Large permanent freshwater lakes
entries.reviewNote: Area, depth, stratification and mixing need explicit units and observation scales; large is an uncalibrated prototype identity.

entries.label: Permanent salt and soda lakes
entries.reviewNote: Salinity, ionic composition and alkalinity need independent measurements; not all saline lakes are soda lakes.

entries.label: Large reservoirs
entries.reviewNote: Water-level operation, residence time, impoundment history and size require context and temporal rules.

entries.label: Rice paddies
entries.reviewNote: Management and inundation cycles vary; the prototype does not impose year-round flooding or a universal wet/dry duration ratio.

entries.label: Permanently open riverine estuaries and bays
entries.reviewNote: Salinity gradients, exchange, freshwater inflow, tides and residence time are more informative than a single brackish identity.

entries.label: Intermittently closed and open lakes and lagoons
entries.reviewNote: Mouth closure cycles can be infrequent or frequent; phase durations and triggers cannot be inferred from the name.

entries.label: Intertidal forests and shrublands
entries.reviewNote: The aggregate mangrove identity includes tree and shrub forms; salinity, thermal limits and sediment dynamics need constraints.

entries.label: Coastal saltmarshes and reedbeds
entries.reviewNote: Freshwater inputs, halophyte traits, tidal exposure and microtopography need explicit scales; a universal salinity value is inappropriate.

entries.label: Rocky Shorelines
entries.reviewNote: Zonation, exposure duration and sessile/mobile biota are omitted; substrate presence does not define the full community.

entries.label: Seagrass meadows
entries.reviewNote: Meadow structure, light, salinity and sediment stabilization need rules; GET includes intertidal examples and occasional rocky substrates.

entries.label: Kelp forests
entries.reviewNote: Light, nutrients, temperature, substrate attachment and herbivory/trophic cascades require more than canopy identity.

entries.label: Photic coral reefs
entries.reviewNote: Symbiosis, light-depth-temperature envelope, salinity and accretion must be modeled; all corals do not define a photic reef.

entries.label: Subtidal mud plains
entries.reviewNote: Deposition, benthic food-web subsidies, oxygen and organic matter need measurable constraints.

entries.label: Epipelagic ocean waters
entries.reviewNote: Photic depth depends on turbidity and season, not a universally fixed depth; pelagic and benthic contexts must remain distinct.

entries.label: Sea ice
entries.reviewNote: Sea ice is not terrestrial snow; freezing, brine channels, seasonal retreat and connected water communities need temporal structure.

entries.label: Chemosynthetic-based-ecosystems (CBE)
entries.reviewNote: Vents, cold seeps and organic falls are alternatives, not mandatory co-occurring components. Pressure and donor chemistry require constraints.

entries.label: Groundwater ecosystems
entries.reviewNote: Aquifer and hyporheic connectivity, residence time, pore space and oxygen need rules; microbial and animal communities vary.

entries.label: Atlantic, Baltic and Arctic sand beach
entries.reviewNote: Regional disjunction is a prototype category; shore processes, tidal setting and community context require review.

entries.label: Mediterranean and Black Sea sand beach
entries.reviewNote: Same material as N11 with a different regional constraint; geography is not evidence of global ecosystem incompatibility.

entries.label: Semi-dry perennial calcareous grassland (meadow steppe)
entries.reviewNote: Diagnostic floristic combinations, substrate chemistry, moisture envelope and management are not replaced by this profile.

entries.label: Lowland to montane, dry to mesic grassland usually dominated by Nardus stricta
entries.reviewNote: Usually dominant is not universally required; dominant taxa, regional assemblages and environmental range need explicit modality.

entries.label: Mesic permanent pasture of lowlands and mountains
entries.reviewNote: Management history and regional vegetation composition are not encoded; generic pasture cover is insufficient.

entries.label: Wet heath
entries.reviewNote: Wetness, peat and characteristic assemblages need diagnostic rules; a single wet observation is not a wet-heath definition.

entries.label: Dry heath
entries.reviewNote: Need a comparable moisture measure and temporal support before treating wet/dry identities as mutually exclusive.

entries.label: Temperate Salix and Populus riparian forest
entries.reviewNote: Willow or poplar is a disjunctive aggregate identity, not a requirement for both; flooding and diagnostics remain unresolved.

entries.label: Fagus forest on non-acid soils
entries.reviewNote: No invented pH cutoff; assemblages and soil/base-status measurements must establish applicability.

entries.label: Fagus forest on acid soils
entries.reviewNote: Shares beech composition with T17; soil acidity and associated diagnostic flora retain the distinction.

entries.label: Mediterranean evergreen Quercus forest
entries.reviewNote: Regional species assemblages and thermomediterranean setting require review; not every evergreen oak stand belongs here.

entries.label: Raised bog
entries.reviewNote: Raised ombrotrophy is narrower than generic GET bog properties, subject to climate and interpretation; no equivalence is asserted.

entries.label: Blanket bog
entries.reviewNote: Blanket versus raised morphology must remain distinct, even if both may fit a broader GET bog group.

entries.label: Poor fen
entries.reviewNote: Poor denotes a context-dependent nutrient/base-status category; it is not an ecosystem condition score.

entries.label: Alkaline, calcareous, carbonate-rich small-sedge spring fen
entries.reviewNote: Alkalinity, carbonate chemistry, peat extent and diagnostic small-sedge assemblages require review; not every spring is this type.

entries.label: Tall-helophyte bed
entries.reviewNote: This class need not have the exact permanence or geomorphic setting of GET permanent marshes.

entries.label: Intensive unmixed crops
entries.reviewNote: Diversity, management intensity and rotation need explicit rules; nominal crop identity is not a GET crosswalk.

entries.label: Agriculturally-improved, re-seeded and heavily fertilised grassland, including sports fields and grass lawns
entries.reviewNote: Includes pasture, sports fields and lawns; the generic managed-herbaceous identity does not impose grazing, and management intensity still needs specification.

entries.label: Atlantic littoral rock
entries.reviewNote: Regional community, exposure and biological zonation require review; source level 3.

entries.label: Mediterranean littoral rock
entries.reviewNote: Comparable to MA12 only after separating biogeography and assemblages; source level 3.

entries.label: Atlantic littoral sand
entries.reviewNote: Grain size, mobile sediments, exposure duration and assemblages need constraints; source level 3.

entries.label: Atlantic littoral mud
entries.reviewNote: Sediment definition, oxygen and estuarine influences are unresolved; source level 3.

entries.label: Atlantic infralittoral rock
entries.reviewNote: Cannot assume every unit is a kelp forest or photic coral reef; source level 3.

entries.label: Mediterranean infralittoral rock
entries.reviewNote: Algal, animal and mixed communities may differ from GET functional groups; source level 3.

entries.label: Seagrass beds on Atlantic littoral sand
entries.reviewNote: Deliberately selected deeper level-4 community to compare with GET M1.1; source level is not inferred from code length.

entries.label: Seagrass beds on Atlantic littoral mud
entries.reviewNote: Level 4; substrate and tidal context refine the seagrass case, subject to consistent meadow/bed interpretation.

entries.label: Seagrass beds on Atlantic infralittoral sand
entries.reviewNote: Level 4; not synonymous with the global seagrass functional group; extent and species assemblages need review.

entries.label: Biocenosis of Posidonia oceanica
entries.reviewNote: Level 4; species identity is an invented stand-in, not an authority-resolved taxon. No numeric taxonomy code is guessed.

entries.label: Atlantic neuston
entries.reviewNote: Level 3; an interface community must not be equated to an entire GET epipelagic water column.

entries.label: Atlantic completely mixed water column with reduced salinity
entries.reviewNote: Level 3; mixing, salinity and seasonality require explicit observation support and thresholds.

entries.label: Atlantic completely mixed water column with full salinity
entries.reviewNote: Level 3; full salinity is a source-relative qualitative category, not an invented universal number.

entries.label: Arctic sea ice
entries.reviewNote: Level 3; freezing, brine, seasonal coverage and sea-ice community require more than frozen cover presence.

entries.label: Permanent oligotrophic lakes, ponds and pools
entries.reviewNote: Trophic status, light, chemistry and water-body extent require measurements; not equivalent to GET large freshwater lakes.

entries.label: Permanent mesotrophic lakes, ponds and pools
entries.reviewNote: No universal nutrient cutoff is invented; the category needs a calibrated observation and temporal support.

entries.label: Permanent eutrophic lakes, ponds and pools
entries.reviewNote: Trophic status is not automatically ecological condition or a pressure score; origin and management must be separated.

entries.label: Permanent inland saline and brackish lakes, ponds and pools
entries.reviewNote: Inland saline and brackish waters need not be soda lakes; ionic composition and ocean connectivity differ from estuaries.

entries.label: Temporary lakes, ponds and pools
entries.reviewNote: Temporary water includes multiple regimes; no fixed hydroperiod duration or generic GET equivalent is assumed.

entries.label: Permanent non-tidal, fast, turbulent watercourses
entries.reviewNote: Not equivalent to upland by itself: stream order, gradient and catchment context are separate properties.

entries.label: Permanent non-tidal, smooth-flowing watercourses
entries.reviewNote: Smooth flow does not by itself determine lowland location, river size or ecosystem functional group.

entries.label: Temporary running waters
entries.reviewNote: GET seasonal upland streams may remain perennial, so this is neither a simple synonym nor an exhaustive mapping.
